body: External tools can extend the capabilities of small language models (SLMs), enabling their deployment in resource constrained environments. However, their limited capabilities make it difficult for SLMs to discover effective tool use behaviors through reinforcement learning alone, while direct teacher supervision suffers from teacher student behavioral distribution mismatch and may propagate erroneous preferences. To address these challenges, we propose Selective Teacher guided Policy Optimization (SeTPO), which coordinates student exploration with selective teacher guidance and persistent demonstration supervision. Specifically, SeTPO incorporates reverse KL derived token level teacher feedback into policy advantages on low reward trajectories, while auxiliary forward KL supervision preserves teacher demonstrated behaviors throughout training. Under an idealized bidirectional KL objective, we theoretically establish that the optimal policy achieves expected reward no lower than the teacher's while retaining a guaranteed fraction of the teacher's probability mass. Extensive experiments on BFCL v4 and API Bank demonstrate that SeTPO achieves superior overall performance over supervised fine tuning, reinforcement learning, and distillation baselines across all three student scales.
summaryZh: 针对小语言模型（SLM）在工具使用能力上的局限性，本文提出了选择性教师引导策略优化（SeTPO）。该方法通过双向KL约束协调学生的探索行为与教师的示范监督，利用反向KL反馈优化低奖励轨迹，并利用前向KL监督保持教师示范行为。实验证明，SeTPO在BFCL v4和API Bank等基准测试中，在工具调用性能上显著优于传统的监督微调与强化学习方法，为资源受限环境下的智能体开发提供了有效路径。
